title: Deeper/broader release-fresh LibreDWG writer and ezdxf ACIS boundaries
mode: primary-source web research and read-only local plan reconciliation
scope: Refresh GNU LibreDWG DWG-writer evidence at its current release boundary
Refresh ezdxf ACIS parsing, export, and mesh-projection limitations
Refine existing optional peer admission without delaying local implementation

method.kind: Read project-owned release history, README, API documentation, and reconcile with the existing plan
method.limitations: The LibreDWG NEWS/README and ezdxf stable documentation are mutable project-owned sources and were not tied to an executed binary or source artifact in this pass. They establish advertised route boundaries only; no peer behavior or libdxfrw conformance was reproduced.

sources.observed: NEWS records R2004/AC1018 DWG writing as a 0.14 feature, while wider R2004+ support is described as started but incomplete; 0.14.1 NEWS records a decompression security fix. The README presents a coarse writer boundary through R2004 rather than a per-class matrix.
sources.limits: No LibreDWG binary, output, independent reopen, per-class status, or native application result was executed.

sources.revision: Stable documentation accessed 2026-10-20; docs identify ezdxf 1.4.5
sources.observed: The ACIS API documents a limited set of known structures, potential loss of unsupported entities loaded as NONE_ENTITY, export refusal for those entities, planar-face-only mesh extraction, and version-specific SAT (R2000-R2010) versus SAB (R2013/R2018) export boundaries.
sources.limits: No ezdxf package was installed or run; documentation does not qualify arbitrary ACIS roundtrip, curved-surface semantics, DWG/AcDs association, or native consumer acceptance.

assessment.planImpact: Refines the existing composed-checkpoint candidate boundaries: LibreDWG 0.14+ is considered only for an exact AC1018 writer question after artifact pinning, and ezdxf only for a fully represented planar ACIS-DXF profile. Continue local implementation without either peer; separate file writing, parsing, graph association, opaque retention, geometric semantics, and native acceptance.

validation.scopedDiffCheck: PASS: git diff --check for the plan and receipt paths
